wordmark.purpose: The lowercase "birdbrain" centred in the header row (28px).

headline.purpose: Column headings, bins and dialog titles, lowercase (20px); the next exam's name at 800.

title.purpose: Today's date, the next exam/quiz labels, Settings section headings (16px, lowercase).

body.purpose: Item titles, form text and the lede, with tabular numerals.

label.purpose: Course codes, dates and chips in the meta line under each item.

window-glyph.purpose: Windows' own icon font for the minimise, maximise and close buttons only (10px).

focus-date.purpose: The Focus layout's headline: today's date, light, 39px.

focus-heading.purpose: Focus column headings, bins and dialog titles, light and lowercase (25px).

shadows.name: frame-bevel
shadows.purpose: The frosted frame and the welcome panel.

shadows.name: lift
shadows.purpose: Hover only, on anything pressable: items, buttons, segmented choices.

shadows.name: scrollbar-float
shadows.purpose: The floating scrollbar thumb, at rest.

shadows.name: chosen-ring
shadows.purpose: The chosen day or night half in the theme picker; shows on any photo.

motion.name: item-hover
motion.purpose: An item takes a faint wash under the pointer; it doesn't move.

motion.name: item-lift
motion.value: 160ms cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1), scale 1.03, Sheet Glass and the Lift shadow
motion.purpose: A ticked item is picked up off the glass while Birdbrain saves.

motion.name: item-flight
motion.value: 460-760ms by distance; x cubic-bezier(.45,0,.3,1), y rises then drops; shrinks to its target
motion.purpose: The item arcs into Completed (its own row if the bin is open, else the heading, else the window edge); Undo flies it home.

motion.name: list-glide
motion.purpose: Items below a ticked one glide up into the gap instead of jumping; new labels fade in.

motion.name: bird-arrives
motion.value: 1.8s on a curved path (offset-path) from the window's top-right edge, cubic-bezier(.25,.1,.25,1), growing as it nears; wings flap every .26s
motion.purpose: When the last thing due today is ticked off, one bird flies in toward the empty all-clear branch. Once a day at most; not with reduced motion.

motion.name: perch-landing
motion.value: 440ms cubic-bezier(.2,.7,.3,1): the perched bird drops from 26px above onto the branch as the flier fades (150ms); the chirp plays at touchdown
motion.purpose: The bird folds its wings and lands.

motion.name: sheet-out
motion.value: .16s cubic-bezier(.4,0,1,1), to opacity 0, translateY 8px, scale .985; the backdrop fades with it
motion.purpose: Dialogs leave the way they came, however they're closed.

motion.name: item-return
motion.value: 420-640ms; y cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1), x cubic-bezier(.4,0,.2,1); no overshoot
motion.purpose: Undo glides an item home, turning a flight around if it's still in the air.

motion.name: layout-veil
motion.value: out 260ms + veil 320ms; in: veil lifts 550ms cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1), list rises 12px
motion.purpose: Switching layout crossfades through the new layout's ground colour instead of flashing on reload.

motion.name: scrollbar
motion.purpose: The scrollbar comes forward and widens.

motion.name: completed-flash
motion.purpose: The Completed heading flashes when an item lands there, only if it's on screen.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Turns off every transition and animation.

narrative.overview:
Birdbrain is a lookout post. The student stands behind a pane of frosted glass and scans the horizon of their week: a real landscape photo (a misted forest, a lavender sky full of birds, a warm-lit cabin, snowy peaks, a pink dusk) fills the window, and everything they need to watch for is written on the glass in front of it. Deadlines that are far off stay quiet and white; the closer something lands, the warmer it glows, until overdue work burns cardinal red. The view changes with the time of day (every theme has a day photo and a night photo) but the pane, the writing and the warning colours never do.

The system is **crisp and legible** first and **warm and cozy** second. Crisp: Atkinson Hyperlegible throughout, white text on glass tinted exactly dark enough to hold contrast over the brightest pixel of each photo, tabular numerals, one clear urgency code. Warm: bird-named heat colours, lowercase headings and italic dates borrowed from the owner's personal site (caseyleblanc.dev, the binding reference for this look), soft rounded glass, a squawk when something new is due and a bird that flies in to land on an empty branch, with a chirp, when today's list is done. Components are **soft glass, quiet until urgent**: items sit clear on the glass with no tile of their own until a deadline or an exam gives them colour and weight, and anything pressable takes a faint wash and rises slightly when the pointer reaches it.

Density is comfortable, not compact: a desktop window with three columns of short tiles, generous gutters, and 44px targets everywhere.
keyCharacteristics: One frosted frame over a full-window photo: a single header row (today's date and counts, the wordmark, the two buttons), a slim strip naming the next exam and quiz, then three glass columns (now, this week, later). The frame can be full width or narrow, letting more of the photo show.
White ink on dark-tinted glass; colour is reserved for urgency (Cardinal, Oriole, Goldfinch) and for exams (the Exam Chip).
Five themes, each a colour scheme with a day and a night photo; the glass tint, title colour, Exam Chip and focus ring change per scheme, the urgency colours never do.

Two layers of glass at most: the frame (blur, a white edge and a light inner bevel) and the flat panels on it. Items are not glass. The only shadows are a slight lift on hover and the floating scrollbar.
Birdbrain draws its own see-through title bar and frosted scrollbar so the photo runs edge to edge.

A second layout, **Focus**, is one calm, roomy page with nothing but the list: the day as the headline, columns straight on a flat canvas with wide space between them and a thin rule down the middle of each gutter, no panels. It speaks Glass's colour language in flat form: the same heat colours for how soon, and chips for exams and quizzes. It has its own nine colour themes, each a different room rather than a tint of one.
Both layouts have a **Custom** theme: your own colours in Focus, your own day and night photos in Glass, held to the same readability rules as the built-in ones.
First run is two short steps: where Moodle and Outlook are, then **make it yours** (layout and theme), with the welcome page itself taking each choice as it's made.

rules.name: The Heat Rule
rules.body: Cardinal, Oriole and Goldfinch mean *when* and nothing else: overdue, today, tomorrow. They never decorate, never mark a type of item, and never appear as text on glass; they are always a solid chip with Chip Ink or a dot, and Cardinal alone may tint a tile. Anything further off than tomorrow is plain text, with no chip at all. Focus keeps the rule in flat form: overdue takes the theme's own red, today and tomorrow Oriole and Goldfinch softened into the canvas, and nothing is tinted.

rules.name: The What-Not-When Rule
rules.body: The Exam Chip says what an item is; the heat colours say when it is due. A tile can carry both, and the two never swap roles.

rules.name: The Measured Glass Rule
rules.body: A scheme's glass tint is set by measurement, not taste: every text on it must reach 4.5:1 (3:1 for window buttons) against the brightest real pixels of that scheme's photo behind it. A new photo means re-measuring, and darkening the tint if it fails.

rules.name: The Five Sizes Rule
rules.body: Text comes in 13, 16, 20, 28 and 40px and nothing in between. Anything more is said with weight, italics or colour.

rules.name: The Lowercase Heading Rule
rules.body: Every heading on glass is lowercase (the title, columns, panels, dialogs, bins), as on caseyleblanc.dev. Item titles, buttons and body copy keep their normal case.

rules.name: The Italic Date Rule
rules.body: Group labels ("monday, sep 28", "tomorrow") and quiet asides (empty states such as "None in the next 30 days.") are italic and soft; dates that need attention become heat chips instead.

rules.name: The Rise-on-Touch Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. A slight shadow appears only when the pointer reaches something pressable, so a shadow always means "you can press this". Panels, columns and read-only text never rise. The one other shadow is on an item in flight to or from Completed, which has been picked up.

rules.name: The Two Panes Rule
rules.body: Glass nests two deep: the frame, then a panel (a column, a bin, the callout strip). Items are never a third pane. They sit clear on the panel, take a wash only under the pointer, and only overdue work is tinted at rest. Nothing sits inside an item except text and chips.

dos: **Do** measure every new photo or glass tint against real pixels: 4.5:1 for text, 3:1 for window buttons (The Measured Glass Rule).
**Do** show urgency as a solid heat chip with Chip Ink (#20140E), a faint tint or a dot, and say it in words too ("overdue", "today", the date).
**Do** keep text on the five sizes (13, 16, 20, 28, 40px) and spacing on multiples of 8px.
**Do** keep headings lowercase and dates italic on glass.
**Do** make every target at least 44px, visibly focusable with the scheme's focus colour, and still usable with reduced motion.
**Do** let pressable glass rise with the Lift shadow on hover, and keep everything else flat.
**Do** keep the urgency colours identical across every scheme and both layouts; change only the glass, title, Exam Chip and focus colour per scheme.
donts: **Don't** set Cardinal, Oriole, Goldfinch or the Exam Chip colour as text on glass; they fail contrast there.
**Don't** use the heat colours for anything but due dates, or the Exam Chip for anything but exams and quizzes.
**Don't** add drop shadows at rest, or give read-only panels a hover shadow.
**Don't** give tiles, panels or callouts a coloured edge or stripe ("card ends").
**Don't** nest glass more than two deep (frame, panel), or give items a fill at rest (The Two Panes Rule).
**Don't** tint an item for anything but overdue work, or chip a date further off than tomorrow.
**Don't** put a badge behind a number, or a default grey dot on a course that has no colour.
**Don't** put text straight on the photo; it always sits on glass.
**Don't** introduce a second display face; Atkinson Hyperlegible carries every role in both layouts.
**Don't** give Focus boxes or shadows at rest, or any rule beyond the thin ones between its columns; its structure is space, a few light headings and those gutter rules.
